newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Safras sees 12.5 mln tonne Argentine soybean crop.
newsitem.headline: Safras sees 12.5 mln tonne Argentine soybean crop.

text.p: Dry weather could mean Argentina's soybean harvest will drop to 12.5 million tonnes, well below initial expectations of between 13.4 million and 14 million tonnes, said independent consultants Safras e Mercado.
A 12.5 million tonne crop would represent a one percent fall on the 12.65 million tonnes harvested in 1995/96, it added in its weekly report.
Planted area however this year is much higher than last at 6.59 million hectares against 5.99 million in 1995/96.
But average productivity is now seen at 1,943 kgs per hectare against 2,144 kgs the previous season.
As of last week, 45.2 percent of the harvest had been collected against 12.5 percent by the same stage last year, accelerated by the dry, hot weather over the past four months.
Argentine soybean exports are now expected to reach 1.3 million tonnes, down 35 percent from the two million sold in the 1996/97 marketing year (April/March).

Soymeal sales overseas are however expected to reach record levels of 8.15 million tonnes against 7.7 million in 1996/97 while soyoil exports are forecast at 1.82 million, up from 1.65 million tonnes last year.
